newsitem.title: USA: Miami sees tourism boost, expects record year.
newsitem.headline: Miami sees tourism boost, expects record year.

text.p: The number of tourists visiting the Miami area rose to 6.44 million for the year through August, a 2.8 percent increase over the same period last year, Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau said Thursday.
At the current rate, the 1996 total would be 9.6 million, surpassing last year's record 9.4 million, the bureau said.
"Barring some last-minute problems, 1996 will go down as our best year ever," said bureau Director Merrett Stierheim.
He said the 1996 totals were expected to exceed those seen before 1993, when Miami tourism dropped due to a highly publicized spate of violent crimes against visitors.
The number of domestic visitors during the first nine months rose to 2.99 million, an increase of 1.75 percent over the same period last year. Visitors from other Southern states led the increase.

The number of international visitors to the Miami area rose to 3.44 million during the first nine months of the year, an increase of 3.7 percent over last year, with European, Canadian and South American visitors leading the influx.
Miami saw a decrease in visitors from the Caribbean islands, whose economies have been hurt by a series of hurricanes.
Tourism officials for the Fort Lauderdale area are also projecting a new record for 1996.
They expect 6.2 million tourists this year compared with 5.4 million last year.
